newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says M0 aggregate up 6.9 pct in May vs Q4.
newsitem.headline: SNB says M0 aggregate up 6.9 pct in May vs Q4.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) said in a preliminary summary of its regular monthly report that its monetary base, M0, grew by 6.9 percent on an annualised basis versus the fourth quarter of 1996.
The SNB said that sight deposits, averaging at 3.728 billion francs, were up 163 million versus the prior month.
The seasonally-adjusted monetary base was up 291 million Swiss francs at 32.850 billion in May versus April.
"Compared with the fourth quarter of 1996, this corresponds to an increase of 3.4 percent. Calculated on the basis of one year, the rate of growth was 6.9 percent," the SNB said.
The SNB's M0 aggregate comprises notes in circulation and sight deposits.
The SNB said as a result of generous additions of liquidity to offset the franc's rise, call money rates fell as low as 0.5 percent in May. Rates also fell on money out to one year.
The SNB already said at a June 19 news conference that the M0 growth rate was nearly seven percent in May.
It also said then the adjusted monetary base was nearly 4.5 percent above its target path calling for growth of one percent per year over a five-year period.

The SNB said on June 19 that some distortions were evident in the aggregate, including a large unexplained increase in notes in circulation. Last year a shift to sight deposits from postal giro accounts also caused M0 to expand. Without such distortions, M0 would be growing more slowly, it said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
